# Apps excluded from the generic compose-boot-test healthcheck-poll job.
#
# Single source of truth — read only by tools/ci/scope/compose_apps.py,
# which feeds:
#   - pr-checks.yml: detect-changes' compose step (compose-boot-test's
#     matrix)
#   - pr-checks.yml: compose-syntax-check (the fallback check for exactly
#     the apps compose-boot-test skips)
#   - boot-test-all.yml: list-apps (compose-boot-test-all's matrix)
#
# One app name per line. Blank lines and full-line '#' comments are
# ignored when this file is parsed; per-app reasoning below stays
# attached to the app it explains.

# bind9, seaweedfs, caddy: already covered by their own molecule
# scenarios with stronger, real-protocol assertions (DNS resolution, S3
# error semantics) than a generic healthcheck poll would add.
bind9
seaweedfs
caddy

# tinyauth: also in that category as of the tinyauth/default Molecule
# scenario (ansible/roles/tinyauth/molecule/default) — it stands up a
# real lldap target and runs lldap_bootstrap for real, exercising
# tinyauth's LdapService bootstrap the way compose-boot-test's
# one-app-per-job isolation never could (see _compose-boot-test.yml: no
# lldap host exists for tinyauth to resolve in that model, regardless of
# config correctness).
tinyauth

# molecule-dind: not a deployed compose app at all — it's CI scaffolding,
# a Dockerfile built and pushed to ghcr.io/wenenhoe/molecule-dind:latest
# for Molecule's DinD scenarios (build-molecule-dind-image.yml). No
# compose.yaml/.j2, so there's nothing for `docker compose up` to run.
molecule-dind

# openbao: can't boot in isolation, so a healthcheck poll can never pass for
# it. Its data volume is chowned to the image's non-root user by roles/openbao
# before the container starts, which the boot-test seeding doesn't do (the
# server dies opening vault.db); its listener needs a leaf cert in the certs
# volume, which this workflow issues only for lldap; and its healthcheck,
# `bao status`, exits non-zero while OpenBao is sealed or uninitialized, as a
# fresh volume always is. It is also a self-managed app
# (compose_self_managed_apps in roles/compose_app), deployed by its own role.
# compose-syntax-check doesn't cover it either: its compose file is a .j2.
openbao
